items.title: Section: Not Belittling Oneself — They Were Once Human Too, and So Am I

items.zh: 唯作是念：彼既是人，漸次修學，於諸菩薩一切學處廣大無量不可思議淨身語等諸律儀戒成就圓滿；我亦是人，漸次修學，決定無疑。當得如彼淨身語等諸律儀戒成就圓滿。
items.en: One simply reflects: those bodhisattvas, being human just as I am, gradually trained themselves, and thereby perfected the vast, boundless, inconceivable pure restraint discipline of body, speech, and mind across every bodhisattva practice. I too am human, and gradually training myself, will without any doubt likewise come to perfect that same pure restraint discipline of body, speech, and mind.

items.title: Section: A Naturally Gentle Disposition — Even Towards the Violent and the Precept-Breaking

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，住律儀戒，常察己過，不伺他非，普於一切兇暴犯戒諸有情所，無損害心，無瞋恚心。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, abiding in restraint discipline, constantly examine their own faults, never searching out others' failings. Towards every violent, precept-breaking being universally, they hold no mind to harm, no mind of resentment.

items.zh: 菩薩於彼由懷上品法大悲故，現前發起深憐愍心、欲饒益心。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, holding a great compassion of the highest order towards that being, directly give rise to a deep sense of pity and a genuine wish to benefit them.

items.title: Section: Enduring Physical Attack Without the Slightest Resentment

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，住律儀戒，雖復遭他手足、塊石、刀杖等觸之所加害，於彼尚無少恚恨心，況當於彼欲出惡言、欲行加害，況復發言毀辱訶責，以少苦觸作不饒益。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, abiding in restraint discipline, even when struck by another's hand, foot, thrown stone, or weapon, hold not the slightest resentment towards them — how much less, then, would they wish to speak harshly or act to harm in return, let alone utter words of insult or reproach, or inflict even the smallest hurt upon them.

items.title: Section: Vigilance Across Past, Present, Future — And Before Any Action Even Begins

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，住律儀戒，具足成就五支所攝不放逸行。一、前際俱行不放逸行，二、後際俱行不放逸行，三、中際俱行不放逸行，四、先時所作不放逸行，五、俱時隨行不放逸行。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, abiding in restraint discipline, fully accomplish vigilance comprised of five aspects: vigilance regarding the past, vigilance regarding the future, vigilance regarding the present, vigilance formed in advance of action, and vigilance sustained throughout action.

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩，於菩薩學正修學時，若於過去已所違犯如法悔除，是名菩薩前際俱行不放逸行。若於未來當所違犯如法悔除，是名菩薩後際俱行不放逸行。若於現在正所違犯如法悔除，是名菩薩中際俱行不放逸行。
若諸菩薩，先於後時當所違犯，發起猛利自誓欲樂：謂我定當如如所應行，如如所應住，如是如是行，如是如是住，令無所犯。是名菩薩先時所作不放逸行。若諸菩薩，即以如是先時所作不放逸行為所依止，如如所應行，如如所應住，如是如是行，如是如是住，不起毀犯。是名菩薩俱時隨行不放逸行。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, before any potential future violation, give rise to an intense, self-made vow of aspiration: I will surely act and dwell exactly as required, precisely in this way, precisely in that way, so that no violation occurs at all. This is called a bodhisattva's vigilance formed in advance of action.

items.title: Section: Proper Conduct and Pure Livelihood — Ten Marks of Restraint Conclude

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，住律儀戒，覆藏自善，發露己惡，少欲喜足，堪忍眾苦，性無憂慼，不掉不躁，威儀寂靜，離矯詐等一切能起邪命之法。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, abiding in restraint discipline, conceal their own virtues, openly confess their own faults, remain content with little, endure every hardship, are naturally free of gloom, are neither restless nor agitated, carry themselves with calm dignity, and are entirely free of deception or any other means that would give rise to improper livelihood.

items.zh: 菩薩成就如是十支，名住律儀戒，善護律儀戒。謂不顧戀過去諸欲，又不希求未來諸欲，又不耽著現在諸欲，又樂遠離不生喜足，又能掃滌不正言論諸惡尋思，又能於己不自輕蔑，又性柔和，又能堪忍，又不放逸，又能具足軌則淨命。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who accomplish these ten marks are said to abide in and skilfully guard restraint discipline: not clinging to past desires, not hoping for future desires, not attached to present desires, delighting in solitude without resting content, clearing away improper talk and unwholesome thought, never belittling themselves, holding a gentle disposition, capable of genuine patience, never negligent, and fully accomplishing proper conduct and pure livelihood.

items.title: Section: Abiding in Wholesome Practice Opens — Progress Through Giving, Discipline, and Patience

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，已能安住攝善法戒。若於身財少生顧戀尚不忍受，何況其多。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, already able to abide in discipline gathering wholesome practice, find even the slightest lingering attachment to body or wealth intolerable — how much more so, then, a greater attachment.

items.zh: 又於一切犯戒因緣根本煩惱、少分煩惱忿恨等生，亦不忍受。又於他所發生恚、害、怨恨等心，亦不忍受。
items.en: Regarding every root affliction that gives rise to violating discipline, or even a lesser affliction such as indignation or lingering resentment, none of it is tolerated the moment it arises. Regarding any hostility, intent to harm, or lingering resentment towards another, none of it is tolerated either.

items.title: Progress Through Diligence and Meditative Concentration

items.zh: 又於所起懈怠、懶惰，亦不忍受。又於所起等至味著、等至煩惱，亦不忍受。
items.en: Regarding any laziness or sluggishness that arises, none of it is tolerated. Regarding any craving for the pleasure of meditative attainment, or any affliction accompanying that attainment, none of it is tolerated either.

items.title: Section: Five Kinds of Wisdom — Seeing Cause, Effect, and Their Distortion Clearly

items.zh: 又於五處如實了知。謂如實知善果勝利，又能如實了知善因，又能如實知善因果倒與無倒，又如實知攝善法障。
items.en: One truly knows five things: truly knowing the supreme benefit of a wholesome fruit; truly knowing its wholesome cause; truly knowing distortion regarding that wholesome cause and effect; truly knowing its absence; and truly knowing what obstructs gathering wholesome practice.

items.zh: 是諸菩薩能於善果見大勝利，尋求善因；為攝善故，如實了知倒與無倒；由此菩薩獲得善果。
不於無常妄見為常，不於其苦妄見為樂，不於不淨妄見為淨，不於無我妄見為我。如實了知攝善法障；為攝善故，速疾遠離。
items.en: Not mistaking what is impermanent for permanent, not mistaking what is suffering for pleasurable, not mistaking what is impure for pure, not mistaking what is without a fixed self for a self — truly recognising what obstructs gathering wholesome practice this way, and for the sake of gathering it, swiftly overcoming that obstruction.

items.title: Section: Abiding in Wholesome Practice Concludes — Ten Marks Named Together

items.zh: 菩薩由此十種相故，名住攝善法戒。速能攝善一切種相。謂施漸次、若戒漸次、若忍漸次、若精進漸次、若靜慮漸次，及五種慧。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, through these ten marks, are said to abide in discipline gathering wholesome practice, swiftly gathering wholesome practice of every kind: progress through giving, progress through discipline, progress through patience, progress through diligence, progress through meditative concentration, and the five kinds of wisdom.

blocks.text: More of the inner life of restraint, then how wholesome practice is gathered.
Hearing of the great bodhisattvas' discipline, one does not lose heart: "those bodhisattvas, being human just as I am, gradually trained themselves. I too am human, and can gradually train myself."

"They examine their own faults, never searching out others'." Towards "every violent, precept-breaking being", they have no hostility, only "great compassion of the highest order". Master Cháng Bǎi: this patience is joined with wisdom, not forced endurance.
"Even when struck by another's hand, foot, stone, or weapon, they hold not the slightest resentment."
Regarding the past (amending past lapses), the future, the present, before acting ("an intense vow: I will act exactly as required"), and while acting.

"They conceal their own virtues, openly confess their faults, are content with little, endure hardship, are naturally free of gloom, neither restless nor deceptive", and so on. Master Cháng Bǎi: deception outwardly and wrong thought within are both excluded.

subs.head: Gathering the good: no tolerance for obstacles

blocks.text: "Even the slightest lingering attachment to body or wealth" is intolerable to them; likewise any anger or resentment, laziness, or craving for meditative pleasure.

Knowing "the supreme benefit of a wholesome fruit; its wholesome cause; distortion regarding them; non-distortion"; and obstacles to them. "Not mistaking the impermanent for permanent, suffering for pleasure, the impure for pure, the selfless for self."

quiz.q: Hearing of the vast discipline of great bodhisattvas, what does one reflect so as not to belittle oneself?
options: they were human and trained gradually; I too am human and, training gradually, will surely attain the same
I'll just recite the Buddha's name
quiz.why: "Those bodhisattvas, being human just as I am, gradually trained themselves… I too am human, and gradually training myself, will without any doubt likewise come to perfect that same pure discipline." Venerable Miào Jìng: those great bodhisattvas were human too — once just like me!

quiz.q: Bodhisattvas hold no harm or resentment towards violent, precept-breaking beings. What kind of patience does Master Cháng Bǎi say this is?
options: patience joined with wisdom, not forced endurance, so it does no harm to oneself
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: this patience is joined with wisdom — not forced endurance — so it does not make one ill. Venerable Miào Jìng: when precept-breakers trouble me, it is not their fault; it happens because of my own past wrongs.

quiz.q: "Before any potential future violation, giving rise to an intense, self-made vow" — which of the five aspects of vigilance is this?
options: vigilance formed in advance of action
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas, before any potential future violation, give rise to an intense, self-made vow of aspiration … This is called a bodhisattva's vigilance formed in advance of action." Master Cháng Bǎi: before walking or standing, the bodhisattva vows not to be negligent.

quiz.q: "Free of deception (jiǎo-zhà) and every means of improper livelihood." How do the lectures distinguish jiǎo and zhà?
options: jiǎo is outward deceptive conduct; zhà is the wrong thinking within
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: jiǎo is deceptive behaviour shown outwardly; zhà is the wrong thinking within. Venerable Miào Jìng says the same.

quiz.q: Bodhisattvas already abiding in the discipline of gathering wholesome practice — how do they treat attachment to body and wealth?
options: even the slightest lingering attachment is intolerable, let alone more
fine as long as one doesn't covet others'
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas … find even the slightest lingering attachment to body or wealth intolerable — how much more so, then, a greater attachment." Master Cháng Bǎi: attachment to the body is self-craving; "progress" means it is achieved gradually — not clinging to body and wealth cannot be done all at once.

quiz.q: "Regarding any laziness or sluggishness that arises, none of it is tolerated." How does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish the two?
options: not sustaining and growing merit already arisen is laziness; not producing good not yet arisen is sluggishness — "don't fear going slowly, only fear standing still"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: failing to sustain and grow merit already arisen is laziness; failing to produce good not yet arisen is sluggishness. "Don't fear slowness, only fear standing still" — content with little, not moving forward, there is no progress.

quiz.q: Through which ten marks are bodhisattvas said to abide in the discipline of gathering wholesome practice?
options: progress through giving, discipline, patience, diligence, and meditative concentration, and the five kinds of wisdom
quiz.why: "Progress through giving, progress through discipline, progress through patience, progress through diligence, progress through meditative concentration, and the five kinds of wisdom." Venerable Miào Jìng: the last are the five kinds of wisdom; the first are five perfections.
